propositions.text: Applicant seeks judicial review of RAD decision dismissing his appeal from RPD rejecting refugee claim
propositions.quote: The Applicant, Jun Zhan, seeks judicial review of the decision of the Refugee Appeal Division [RAD], dismissing his appeal from the decision of the Refugee Protection Division [RPD] that rejected his claim for refugee protection.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant seeks judicial review of RAD decision dismissing his appeal from RPD rejecting refugee claim, court states.

propositions.text: Applicant concedes passport evidence discrepancy but says it's peripheral
propositions.quote: The Applicant concedes that there was a discrepancy in his evidence regarding his passport (and former passport), but he submits this is a peripheral matter.

propositions.text: Applicant challenges RAD's credibility findings and says RAD failed to assess core element of claim about Falun Gong adherence
propositions.quote: He challenges the RAD’s credibility findings and says that it failed to assess the core element of his claim relating to his adherence to Falun Gong.

propositions.text: Applicant contends RAD's failure to analyze essential aspect of claim makes decision unreasonable
propositions.quote: The Applicant contends that the RAD’s failure to analyze this essential aspect of his refugee claim makes its decision unreasonable.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant concedes passport discrepancy but says peripheral, challenges RAD credibility findings and failure to assess core Falun Gong claim, says decision unreasonable.

propositions.text: Court disagrees, finds RAD's credibility findings reasonable and clearly explained
propositions.quote: I do not agree. The RAD made several credibility findings, listed below, which added up to undermine his overall credibility. Its conclusion that he had failed to establish that he is a genuine practitioner of Falun Gong is based on the evidence, clearly explained, and reasonable.

paragraphs.summary: Court disagrees with applicant, finds RAD's credibility findings reasonable and clearly explained.

propositions.text: Application for judicial review will be dismissed
propositions.quote: For these reasons, the application for judicial review will be dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: Court dismisses application for judicial review.

propositions.text: Applicant is Chinese citizen fearing persecution for Falun Gong practice, fled to Canada in 2018
propositions.quote: The Applicant is a citizen of China, who says he fled the country fearing persecution from police and public security authorities because of his practice of Falun Gong.

propositions.text: Applicant began Falun Gong after friend told him of health benefits
propositions.quote: He states that he began to practice Falun Gong after a friend told him about the health benefits.

propositions.text: Applicant saw police outside Falun Gong group location, then went into hiding
propositions.quote: One day, he saw a police car outside of the location where his Falun Gong group practiced and then went into hiding.

propositions.text: Several group members arrested, another in hiding
propositions.quote: He learned that several of the group members had been arrested, and another member was in hiding.

propositions.text: Applicant obtained visitor visa with smuggler's help, arrived Canada August 2018, claimed refugee status
propositions.quote: With the assistance of a smuggler, the Applicant says he obtained a visitor’s visa to Canada; he arrived in August 2018 and claimed refugee status.

propositions.text: Applicant's sister advised him PSB officers visited his home in China asking about his location
propositions.quote: Subsequent to his arrival, the Applicant was advised by his sister that officers from the Public Security Bureau [PSB] visited his home in China several times asking about his location.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant is Chinese citizen fearing persecution for Falun Gong, fled to Canada in 2018, police visited his home in China.

propositions.text: RPD rejected claim finding lack of credibility about Falun Gong practice
propositions.quote: The RPD rejected the Applicant’s claim, finding that his claim to be a Falun Gong practitioner lacked credibility.

propositions.text: RAD disagreed with some RPD credibility findings but dismissed appeal on its own credibility assessment
propositions.quote: On appeal, the RAD disagreed with certain of the RPD’s credibility findings, but nevertheless dismissed the appeal based on its own assessment of the Applicant’s credibility.

propositions.text: Key RAD findings discussed below in judicial review analysis
propositions.quote: The key findings of the RAD are discussed below, in the context of the analysis of the Applicant’s submissions on judicial review.

paragraphs.summary: RPD rejected claim for lack of credibility; RAD disagreed with some RPD findings but dismissed appeal on credibility; key RAD findings discussed below.

propositions.text: Issue is whether RAD decision is reasonable under Vavilov framework
propositions.quote: The only issue in this case is whether the RAD’s decision is reasonable. This is to be assessed in accordance with the framework set out by the Supreme Court of Canada in Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v Vavilov, 2019 SCC 65 [Vavilov].

paragraphs.summary: Issue is whether RAD decision is reasonable under Vavilov framework, court states.

propositions.text: Reasonable decision is internally coherent, rational, justified in relation to facts and law
propositions.quote: a reasonable decision is “one that is based on an internally coherent and rational chain of analysis and that is justified in relation to the facts and law that constrain the decision maker” (Vavilov at para 85).

propositions.text: Administrative decision must be justified, intelligible and transparent
propositions.quote: An administrative decision-maker’s exercise of public power must be “justified, intelligible and transparent” (Vavilov at para 95).

propositions.text: Applicant must show flaws in decision that are sufficiently central or significant
propositions.quote: The onus is on the Applicant to demonstrate flaws in the decision that are “sufficiently central or significant” (Vavilov at para 100).

paragraphs.summary: Vavilov requires reasonable decisions to be coherent, justified, transparent; applicant must show central flaws.

propositions.text: Decision assessed in light of history, context, evidence and submissions
propositions.quote: The decision should be assessed in light of the history and context of the proceedings, including the evidence and submission made to the decision-maker (Vavilov at para 94).

propositions.text: Reviewing court should not interfere with factual findings absent exceptional circumstances
propositions.quote: A reviewing court should not interfere with a decision-maker’s factual findings “absent exceptional circumstances” (Vavilov at para 125).

propositions.text: Failure to grapple with key issues or central arguments may render decision unreasonable
propositions.quote: a decision-maker’s failure to “meaningfully grapple with key issues or central arguments raised by the parties” may render a decision unreasonable (Vavilov at para 128).

paragraphs.summary: Vavilov says decisions assessed in context; courts defer factual findings unless exceptional; failure to address key issues may be unreasonable.

propositions.text: Applicant argues RAD decision unreasonable on four elements, court will analyze each
propositions.quote: The Applicant argues that the RAD decision is unreasonable, focusing on four elements, listed below. Under each heading, I will briefly summarize the RAD’s findings, then the Applicant’s submissions, followed by my analysis of each.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues RAD decision unreasonable on four elements; court will analyze each.

propositions.text: RPD and RAD found passport discrepancies undermined Applicant's credibility
propositions.quote: A key finding by both the RPD and the RAD was that discrepancies between the documentary evidence and the Applicant’s testimony about the passport he used to travel to Canada and his previous international travel undermined his credibility.

propositions.text: Applicant testified passport was genuine and Canada trip was only international travel
propositions.quote: The Applicant testified that this passport was genuine, and that his trip to Canada was his only international travel.

propositions.text: RPD noted passport had notation showing it replaced previous passport which showed travel to Brunei
propositions.quote: The RPD pointed out that this version of the Applicant’s passport contained an official notation indicating that it was a replacement for a previous passport and included the number of that original passport. A copy of the previous passport had been included with the Applicant’s application for a Canadian visitor’s visa, and it showed that he had previously travelled to Brunei.

paragraphs.summary: RPD and RAD found passport discrepancies undermined credibility; passport showed prior travel to Brunei.

propositions.text: RPD did not find Applicant's explanation that earlier passport was forged credible
propositions.quote: The RPD did not find his explanation to be credible, and found that his testimony undermined his credibility.

propositions.text: Applicant said he did not know about earlier passport and claimed smuggler forged it
propositions.quote: When questioned by the RPD about this, the Applicant stated that he did not know anything about this, that the earlier passport was forged by the smuggler and that he had no clue about the indication that he had travelled to Brunei.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant claimed earlier passport forged by smuggler; RPD found explanation not credible and undermined credibility.

propositions.text: RAD not persuaded by Applicant's explanation, found passport genuine and replaced previous one to conceal travel
propositions.quote: The RAD was also not persuaded by the Applicant’s explanation on this point, noting that he had testified that the passport was genuine and had been issued before his involvement with Falun Gong and the smuggler. The RAD concluded that the passport could be relied on for the truth of its contents, including the notation that it was a replacement for a previous passport. Based on this, and considering the Applicant’s testimony on this point, the RAD stated: From this, it would appear that the [Applicant’s] claims of not ever having more than one passport or leaving China prior to coming to Canada are falsehoods and, on a balance of probability, I find that that [Applicant] had his previous passport cancelled and replaced by the one dated May 29, 2018, in order to conceal his prior international travel to Brunei, and that it is for this same reason that he continues to deny the authenticity of the original passport.

paragraphs.summary: RAD found passport genuine, replaced previous one to conceal prior travel, and Applicant's denials were falsehoods.

propositions.text: RAD drew negative credibility inference from passport issue, found it showed willingness to mislead
propositions.quote: The RAD drew a negative credibility inference from this, and found that although this was not determinative of his credibility, it was an appropriate consideration because it was not a trivial matter. Instead, the RAD found it demonstrated the Applicant’s apparent ongoing willingness to mislead the Board.

paragraphs.summary: RAD found passport issue showed willingness to mislead and negatively affected credibility though not determinative.

propositions.text: Applicant concedes inconsistency reasonable but peripheral to core refugee claim
propositions.quote: At the hearing, the Applicant conceded that the RAD’s finding of an inconsistency was reasonable, but claimed that this was a peripheral matter that did not address the core of his refugee claim about persecution because he is an adherent of Falun Gong.

propositions.text: Applicant acknowledges inconsistency could affect overall credibility
propositions.quote: The Applicant acknowledged that this inconsistency could affect his overall credibility.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant concedes passport inconsistency reasonable but peripheral, acknowledges it could affect overall credibility.

propositions.text: Respondent argues Applicant's untruthfulness is major blow to credibility and central to RAD analysis
propositions.quote: On this point, the Respondent argued that it is important to consider the ramifications of this finding (and the concession): the Applicant acknowledged being untruthful before the Board, and he persisted in that conduct after the discrepancies were pointed out to him. By any measure, according to the Respondent, this is a major blow to the Applicant’s credibility and it was a central foundation of the RAD’s analysis.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues Applicant's untruthfulness is major blow to credibility and central to RAD's analysis.

propositions.text: Court agrees with Respondent that Applicant's untruthfulness undermines credibility and is not peripheral
propositions.quote: I agree with the Respondent on this point. The Applicant has conceded that he was not truthful in the evidence he put before the Board. While this evidence did not directly address the core of his refugee claim, it is hardly peripheral since his passport is a basic identity document, he used it to flee China (which is discussed below), and the Applicant’s testimony about it was found to be completely untruthful. The RAD reasonably concluded that this undermined the Applicant’s credibility.

paragraphs.summary: Court agrees with Respondent that Applicant's untruthfulness undermines credibility and is not peripheral.

propositions.text: Applicant testified police came to his home seeking to arrest and search shortly after he left China
propositions.quote: The RAD noted that during the RPD hearing, the Applicant testified that the police had come to his home in China seeking to arrest him and to search his home shortly after he left the country.

propositions.text: Applicant said he did not include this in Basis of Claim form because he had not thought about it
propositions.quote: When the RPD questioned him about why he had not included these details in his Basis of Claim form or his Addendum, the Applicant stated he had not thought about it.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant testified police came to his home seeking arrest and search after he left China; he did not include this in claim form as he had not thought about it.

propositions.text: RAD rejected Applicant's explanation that he was not required to provide encyclopaedic detail
propositions.quote: The RAD rejected the Applicant’s claim that his explanation should have been accepted because he could not be expected to know how much to include in his BOC and that he was not required to provide “encyclopaedic detail” in his narrative.

propositions.text: RAD found police visit was seminal detail establishing threat and should have been included
propositions.quote: The RAD found that this evidence was not a minor matter, but rather was “a – if not the – seminal detail in establishing the threat he faces in China, as he is wanted by the police.” (RAD Decision at para 18). As such, the RAD found it was exactly the sort of material information that should have been recorded in the Applicant’s narrative because it “most establishes the danger that he claims to face.”

propositions.text: Applicant unable to provide general info about when he first learned police visited his home
propositions.quote: In addition, the RAD noted that the Applicant had been unable to provide even general information about when he first learned that the police had come to his house.

paragraphs.summary: RAD rejected Applicant's explanation, found police visit was seminal threat detail and should have been included; Applicant unable to say when he learned of visit.

propositions.text: RAD found Applicant was embellishing evidence about police visit and not truthful
propositions.quote: Given all of the above, I find, on a balance of probabilities, that the Appellant was not being truthful, but rather embellishing his evidence by adding this account – for the first time – in his testimony at the hearing.

propositions.text: RAD found this undermined Applicant's credibility and allegations of police pursuit
propositions.quote: I find that this, too, undermines the credibility of the Appellant and his allegations of being pursued by the police.

propositions.text: RAD found this finding significant as it goes to heart of claim and undermines entire claim foundation
propositions.quote: That these allegations have been significantly undermined throws into doubt not only the allegations of pursuit, but also the foundation of the Appellant’s entire claim.

paragraphs.summary: RAD found Applicant embellished police visit evidence, undermining credibility and the foundation of his claim.

propositions.text: RAD misunderstood RPD's finding about omission; he mentioned police visit in BOC Addendum
propositions.quote: The Applicant submits that the RAD misunderstood the RPD’s finding regarding the nature of the omission. Contrary to the RAD’s finding, he says that he had mentioned the police visit in his BOC Addendum.

propositions.text: Applicant argues inability to recall exact timing is inconsequential and should not affect credibility
propositions.quote: Similarly, he argues that the fact that he could not recall exactly when he learned of these visits should not weigh against his credibility because this is an inconsequential detail.

propositions.text: Failure to provide specific date does not undermine evidence that visits happened
propositions.quote: his failure to provide such specific information does not call into question his evidence that such visits happened.

propositions.text: RAD's findings amount to unreasonably microscopic analysis and erroneous negative inference
propositions.quote: The Applicant contends that the RAD’s findings on this point amount to an unreasonably microscopic analysis, and that it erred in drawing a negative inference from his evidence on this point.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues RAD misunderstood RPD's omission finding, that timing detail is inconsequential, and RAD erred by negative inference from his evidence.

propositions.text: Applicant is reiterating failed arguments; RAD reasonably addressed late narrative addition and credibility
propositions.quote: The Respondent contends that the Applicant is simply reiterating the arguments that failed to sway the RAD. Overall, the Respondent submits that the RAD reasonably and comprehensively dealt with the Applicant’s arguments regarding this late addition to his narrative, and that this is one more reasonable credibility finding that added to the cumulative total that combined to undermine the Applicant’s overall credibility.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent says Applicant repeats failed arguments; RAD reasonably addressed late narrative and credibility issues.

propositions.text: Disagrees with Applicant; RAD considered BOC Addendum and reasonably found testimony undermined credibility
propositions.quote: I do not agree with the Applicant that the RAD failed to take account of this BOC Addendum, and the RAD’s conclusion that his testimony on this question undermined his credibility was reasonable.

paragraphs.summary: Court disagrees with Applicant; finds RAD reasonably considered BOC Addendum and credibility.

propositions.text: RAD mentioned BOC Addendum dated October 16, 2020, so did not ignore evidence
propositions.quote: The RAD specifically mentioned that the Applicant had filed a BOC Addendum, dated October 16, 2020 (see paras 16 and 18), and so it cannot be said to have ignored this evidence.

propositions.text: Review of BOC Addendum confirms RAD's analysis is reasonable
propositions.quote: On the contrary, a review of the BOC Addendum confirms that the RAD’s analysis is reasonable.

propositions.text: BOC Addendum states police came to look for Applicant at home many times; daughter told him but not when or how many
propositions.quote: 3. As well, since arriving in Canada, the police have come to look for me at my house. My daughter has told me that they have come to my house many times to locate me but she did not tell me when or how many exactly.

propositions.text: Daughter tells police she lost contact with Applicant
propositions.quote: She also told me that she tells the police that she lost contact with me.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RAD mentioned BOC Addendum and its analysis reasonable; Addendum states police came many times to Applicant's home.

propositions.text: BOC Addendum's general statement contrasts with Applicant's testimony police came on August 30, 2018
propositions.quote: The generality of this statement stands in contrast to the Applicant’s testimony that the police had come to his home seeking to arrest him on August 30, 2018.

propositions.text: RAD reasonably noted omission of arrest detail from BOC and Addendum was unreasonable given counsel representation
propositions.quote: The RAD reasonably noted that this detail was omitted from the BOC and BOC Addendum, and that it was not reasonable that he would not have thought to include such a central element of his claim, in particular because he was represented by counsel.

propositions.text: RAD found this evidence central to refugee claim as Applicant fled fearing persecution for Falun Gong practice
propositions.quote: The RAD also found that this evidence went to the heart of the Applicant’s refugee claim, since he says he fled China fearing persecution by the authorities because of his practice of Falun Gong.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds BOC Addendum general, contrasts with specific testimony; RAD reasonably noted omission and centrality to claim.

propositions.text: No basis to question RAD's conclusion; late addition of crucial fact undermined credibility
propositions.quote: I can find no basis to question the RAD’s conclusion on this point. This late addition of a crucial fact was not satisfactorily explained by the Applicant, and the RAD reasonably found that it undermined his credibility.

propositions.text: Omission of arrest details from BOC was key evidence supporting fear of persecution; mentioning only at testimony diminishes credibility
propositions.quote: The details he omitted from his BOC form about the arrest were key evidence that supported his claimed fear of persecution, and it was reasonable to find that only mentioning them during his testimony diminish his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds no basis to question RAD; late addition of key fact undermined credibility as omission was key evidence.

propositions.text: RPD found it illogical police would continue searching after Applicant left using own passport and authorities knew departure
propositions.quote: The RPD found that it was not logical that the police would continue to search for the Applicant after his departure, given that he had used his own passport when leaving the country and authorities would have known that he had departed because China has such strict exit controls and authorities have access to so much information.

paragraphs.summary: RPD found police continuing search after Applicant's departure illogical due to strict exit controls and passport use.

propositions.text: RAD upheld RPD finding; Applicant did not challenge it in appeal; RAD agreed with RPD analysis
propositions.quote: The RAD upheld this finding, noting that the Applicant had not challenged it in his appeal submissions, and also that it agreed with the substance of the RPD’s analysis.

paragraphs.summary: RAD upheld RPD's finding; Applicant did not challenge it; RAD agreed with RPD's analysis.

propositions.text: Applicant argues RAD's finding is unreasonable speculation; no proof authorities knew departure or why family harassed
propositions.quote: The Applicant argues that this is unreasonable speculation. The RAD had no way of knowing whether authorities would have actually obtained the information about his departure, or why they might continue to harass his family even if he had left.

propositions.text: Applicant notes PSB came seeking his whereabouts, different from coming to find him
propositions.quote: He also noted that the PSB came to his house seeking his whereabouts, which is different than coming to find him there.

propositions.text: Applicant submits it is plausible authorities would question family due to suspicions from his departure
propositions.quote: On this reading of the evidence, the Applicant submits that it was entirely plausible that Chinese authorities would come to his house to question his family members, because his departure from China would probably raise suspicions about his activities and location.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues RAD's finding is speculation; no proof authorities knew departure or why family harassed; plausible authorities questioned family.

propositions.text: Applicant cannot raise argument on judicial review as he did not challenge RPD finding in RAD appeal
propositions.quote: The Respondent submits that this argument cannot be accepted because the Applicant did not challenge the RPD’s finding in his RAD appeal. It cannot be raised for the first time on judicial review, according to the Respondent.

propositions.text: RPD and RAD findings reasonable; Applicant's argument that departure raises suspicion but police still look for him makes no sense
propositions.quote: In addition, the Respondent says that the RPD’s and RAD’s findings on this point are reasonable. In its written memorandum, the Respondent makes the following submission: “the Applicant’s argument that his departure would, on the one hand, raise police suspicions (i.e. he concedes they were aware that he had left the country), but on the other, they would still look for him, makes no sense and does not show an error.” (Respondent’s Factum at para 35).

paragraphs.summary: Respondent says Applicant cannot raise argument on judicial review; RPD and RAD findings reasonable; Applicant's argument illogical.

propositions.text: Agrees Applicant's argument fails as he did not challenge RPD findings in RAD appeal and raised argument on non-existent RPD finding
propositions.quote: I agree with the Respondent that the Applicant’s argument on this point must fail because he did not challenge the RPD’s findings in his RAD appeal, but rather he raised an argument about a finding that the RPD did not actually make.

propositions.text: Applicant argued RPD erred in finding implausible his departure using own passport; RAD noted RPD did not find this
propositions.quote: In his RAD submissions, the Applicant argued that the RPD had erred in finding it to be implausible that he had been able to leave China using his own passport. As the RAD correctly noted, this is not, in fact, what the RPD found and so it did not address this argument.

paragraphs.summary: Court agrees Applicant's argument fails as he did not challenge RPD findings and raised argument on non-existent RPD finding.

propositions.text: Agrees partially with Applicant that RAD's plausibility conclusion is questionable
propositions.quote: On the substance of the matter, I agree to a degree with the Applicant’s submission that to the extent this is a plausibility finding, the RAD’s conclusion is questionable.

propositions.text: RAD did not make general plausibility finding but considered evidence in overall claim context
propositions.quote: However, upon a closer examination, I find that the RAD did not make a general plausibility finding, but rather considered the Applicant’s evidence in the context of his overall claim.

propositions.text: RPD set out evidence on Chinese government's tracking and exit controls, including biometrics and tracking of Falun Gong practitioners
propositions.quote: The RPD set out the evidence regarding the tracking and control mechanisms used by the Chinese government, including its strict exit controls, which are aided by the biometrics embedded in its official passports. It also noted that such information is available to police officials and the system has been used to track down Falun Gong practitioners.

propositions.text: RPD found Applicant's claim police came many times to home was not credible and embellishment to bolster claim
propositions.quote: Based on this, the RPD found that the Applicant’s claim that police had come to his home searching for him on many occasions was not credible, and that it was an embellishment to bolster his claim.

paragraphs.summary: Court partly agrees RAD's plausibility conclusion questionable but finds RAD considered evidence contextually; RPD found police visits claim not credible.

propositions.text: RAD agreed with RPD's analysis and found it undermined Applicant's credibility about PSB visits
propositions.quote: On appeal, the RAD agreed with the RPD’s analysis and found that this undermined the Applicant’s credibility of the claims that the PSB has repeatedly sought him at his home in China.

paragraphs.summary: RAD agreed with RPD and found Applicant's credibility undermined regarding PSB visits claim.

propositions.text: Finding based largely on evidence of Chinese government's tracking and exit controls, which Applicant does not dispute
propositions.quote: Two things should be noted about this finding: first, it is largely based on the evidence about the nature and extent of the Chinese government’s tracking system and strict exit controls, and the Applicant takes no issue with that.

propositions.text: RAD found Applicant's evidence was police came many times seeking to find him; no evidence family was questioned or pressured
propositions.quote: Second, the RAD’s specific finding is that the Applicant’s evidence, set out in his BOC Addendum and his testimony, was that the PSB had come to his home on many occasions, seeking to find him. ... There is no evidence that the Applicant’s daughter or other family members were questioned at length or otherwise pressured to disclose the Applicant’s specific location; instead, he says the police came looking for him.

propositions.text: RPD and RAD concluded it was unreasonable police would come looking given exit control info showing Applicant departed
propositions.quote: This is the basis for the RPD’s and RAD’s conclusion that it was not reasonable to think that the police would have done this, given their ready access to the exit control information that would show he had departed the country.

paragraphs.summary: Court notes finding based on undisputed tracking evidence; no evidence family pressured; RAD and RPD found police visits unreasonable given exit info.

propositions.text: On evidence and case context, RAD's conclusions on police visits are reasonable
propositions.quote: On the specific evidence before it, and in the context of the case as a whole, I find the RAD’s conclusions on this point to be reasonable.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RAD's conclusions on police visits reasonable given evidence and case context.

propositions.text: RAD found Applicant failed to establish genuine Falun Gong practice or risk from activities in Canada
propositions.quote: The RAD found that the Applicant had failed to establish that he is a genuine Falun Gong practitioner and to demonstrate that his Falun Gong activities in Canada supported a finding that he was at risk of persecution if he returned to China.

propositions.text: Applicant tendered almost no specific evidence of Falun Gong activities or publicity in Canada
propositions.quote: The RAD found that the Applicant had tendered almost no specific evidence with respect to his Falun Gong activities in Canada, nor did he provide any evidence of any sort of publicity or coverage of his activities here.

propositions.text: RAD concluded no evidence Chinese authorities aware of Applicant's activities in Canada
propositions.quote: Given this, even if one were to accept that the Chinese authorities engage in some sort of widespread monitoring of overseas Falun Gong activities, there has been no indication or evidence tendered to indicate that accounts of the [Applicant’s] activities have appeared in the public realm or media, which begs the question of how the authorities he fears could have become aware of is activities in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: RAD found Applicant failed to prove genuine Falun Gong practice or risk in Canada; no evidence of publicity or awareness by Chinese authorities.

propositions.text: Applicant says RAD ignored ample evidence of Chinese monitoring of Falun Gong including photos and spy allegations
propositions.quote: The Applicant submits that the RAD ignored the ample documentary evidence about the extent to which China monitors Falun Gong practitioners, including information from Canadian representatives. This includes taking photographs of Falun Gong protesters at overseas embassies, and allegations that government spies monitor such activities and report back.

propositions.text: Applicant argues RAD applied wrong test; question is reasonable chance of persecution, not awareness of activities
propositions.quote: The Applicant argues that the RAD applied the wrong test: the question is not whether the Applicant’s practice of Falun Gong in Canada has come to the attention of Chinese authorities, but rather whether there is a reasonable chance that he would face persecution due to his association with the practice in Canada.

propositions.text: Applicant contends RAD failed to realistically assess Chinese info collection and monitoring of his activities
propositions.quote: The Applicant contends that the RAD was not able to undertake a realistic assessment of what information Chinese authorities collect in Canada and whether his religious activities were being monitored by the Chinese government.

propositions.text: Applicant submits RAD's finding on sur place claim is unreasonable
propositions.quote: Because of this, the Applicant submits that the RAD’s finding is unreasonable.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues RAD ignored evidence of Chinese monitoring, applied wrong test, failed realistic assessment, and made unreasonable finding.

propositions.text: Respondent says RAD engaged with evidence and reasonably concluded Applicant lacked credible sur place claim
propositions.quote: The Respondent submits that the RAD engaged with the evidence, considered the documentary evidence about the Chinese government’s monitoring of overseas activities as well as the photographic evidence submitted by the Applicant, and reasonably concluded that he did not have a credible sur place claim.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent says RAD engaged evidence and reasonably concluded Applicant lacked credible sur place claim.

propositions.text: Court agrees with Respondent; RAD conducted nuanced review and found lack of specificity and public evidence
propositions.quote: I agree with the Respondent’s argument. The RAD conducted a nuanced and thorough review of the evidence of he sur place claim. The Applicant does not mention the RAD’s findings regarding the lack of specificity in his evidence about his activities in Canada, or the absence of evidence that any of the photographs he submitted had become publicly available.

propositions.text: Lack of specificity and absence of public evidence core to RAD's conclusion; no basis to find unreasonable
propositions.quote: These findings are core to the RAD’s overall conclusion on this point, and I can find no basis to find them to be unreasonable.

propositions.text: Applicant did not provide sufficient evidence; RAD's conclusion based on evidence and explained clearly; reasonable
propositions.quote: The Applicant did not provide sufficient evidence to support his sur place claim, and the RAD’s conclusion is based on the evidence that he did bring forward, as well as its assessment of the documentary evidence. The conclusion is also explained in clear terms. It is reasonable.

paragraphs.summary: Court agrees RAD thoroughly reviewed sur place claim, found lack of evidence, and made reasonable conclusion.

propositions.text: Application for judicial review dismissed; RAD's analysis meets reasonableness test
propositions.quote: For all of the reasons set out above, the application for judicial review will be dismissed. The RAD’s analysis meets the reasonableness test,

propositions.text: RAD's credibility findings cumulatively undermine Applicant's claim; analysis based on evidence and responsive to submissions
propositions.quote: and its findings on each of the credibility issues discussed above, as well as others mentioned in its decision, added up to undermine the credibility of the Applicant’s claim. The RAD’s analysis is based in the evidence and responsive to the Applicant’s submissions on appeal.

propositions.text: Findings clearly explained; meets reasonableness standard
propositions.quote: The findings are clearly explained. That is all that reasonableness requires.

paragraphs.summary: Court dismisses judicial review; finds RAD's analysis reasonable, evidence-based, responsive, and clearly explained.

propositions.text: Applicant's other arguments about the RAD decision were not addressed at hearing and are unpersuasive
propositions.quote: The Applicant’s written submissions set out a number of other arguments about the RAD decision, but these were not addressed during the hearing. I would add that I am not persuaded by any of these other claims.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Applicant's other arguments about the RAD decision unpersuasive and not addressed at hearing.

propositions.text: Applicant's general submission that RAD failed to make determinative findings on genuine Falun Gong adherence is unpersuasive
propositions.quote: I am also not persuaded by the Applicant’s more general submission that the RAD failed to make determinative findings on whether he is a genuine adherent of Falun Gong, which lies at the heart of his refugee claim.

propositions.text: RAD found Applicant failed to establish he is a genuine Falun Gong practitioner based on negative credibility findings
propositions.quote: Based on the accumulated weight of the negative credibility findings it made, the RAD found that the Applicant had failed to establish that he is a genuine Falun Gong practitioner (RAD Decision at para 30).

propositions.text: Applicant agrees RAD decision lacks much analysis of his knowledge of Falun Gong but argues this is fatal
propositions.quote: While I agree with the Applicant that the decision does not contain much analysis of the Applicant’s knowledge of Falun Gong, this is not fatal, given the other findings made by the RAD.

propositions.text: RAD noted Applicant did not provide detailed evidence about his practice or its significance
propositions.quote: On this point, it should be mentioned that the RAD notes at several points in its decision that the Applicant did not provide detailed evidence regarding his practice or about its significance in this life.

propositions.text: RAD's conclusion that Applicant failed to establish he is an adherent of Falun Gong is clear and reasonable
propositions.quote: The RAD’s conclusion that the Applicant failed to establish that he is an adherent of Falun Gong is both clear and reasonable.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Applicant's submission that RAD failed to make determinative findings on Falun Gong adherence unpersuasive, agreeing RAD's conclusion is clear and reasonable.

propositions.text: Application for judicial review is dismissed
propositions.quote: For the reasons set out above, the application for judicial review will be dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the application for judicial review.

propositions.text: No question of general importance for certification
propositions.quote: There is no question of general importance for certification.

propositions.text: Judgment is that application for judicial review is dismissed
propositions.quote: THIS COURT’S JUDGMENT is that: The application for judicial review is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the application and finds no question of general importance for certification.
